title: Balanced scalar associativity for ideal-quotient towers
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b V$ be maps of sheaves of commutative rings. Use module sheaves, their sheafified tensor products and unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let $I_{n+1}\subseteq I_n\subseteq R$, $n\geq1$, be ideal subsheaves, and let $J_n=a(I_n)S$ and $K_n=(ba)(I_n)V$ be the ideal subsheaves locally generated by their indicated images. Here ideal products and ring quotients are sheafified constructions [def-weil-pbc-ideal-module-quotients]; in particular $b(J_n)V=K_n$. Write $E_a=-\otimes_R S$, $E_b=-\otimes_S V$, $E_{ba}=-\otimes_R V$, applied termwise to complexes. For a complex $P$ put $X_R(P)_n=P\otimes_R R/I_n$; define $X_S$ and $X_V$ analogously with $J_n$ and $K_n$, with the quotient transitions [def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $\alpha_P:E_bE_aP\xrightarrow\sim E_{ba}P$ be the balanced associator $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\mapsto p\otimes b(s)q$.

There are natural isomorphisms of complexes of strict towers
$$\beta_a^P:E_aX_R(P)\xrightarrow\sim X_S(E_aP),\quad
\beta_b^M:E_bX_S(M)\xrightarrow\sim X_V(E_bM),\quad
\beta_{ba}^P:E_{ba}X_R(P)\xrightarrow\sim X_V(E_{ba}P).$$
The first is specified on local tensor generators by
$$((p\otimes\bar r)\otimes s)\longmapsto (p\otimes s)\otimes\overline{a(r)},$$
and the other two by the same formula for their ring maps. These are formulas on images in sheafifications, not assertions that tensor sheaves or quotient sheaves are computed on sections. They satisfy the strict tower equation
$$X_V(\alpha_P)\,\beta_b^{E_aP}\,E_b(\beta_a^P)
=\beta_{ba}^P\,\alpha_{X_R(P)}.$$
Each $\beta$ carries the scalar extension of the quotient augmentation $p\mapsto p\otimes\bar1$ to the corresponding quotient augmentation. For an identity ring map, multiplication identifies $\beta$ with the identity. All assertions are natural for cochain maps, use the actual quotient transitions, and require no flatness, finite rank or boundedness hypothesis. No completion or derived limit occurs.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: sheafified tensor formulas; agent-formulated quotient-tower scalar associativity extracted from original coherence proof Steps 1 and 4.

proof.text: For any ring-sheaf map $c:A\to B$, any $A$-module sheaf $F$, and any $B$-module sheaf $H$, an $A$-linear map $f:F\to\operatorname{Res}_cH$ extends uniquely to a $B$-linear map $\widetilde f:E_cF\to H$: on the sectionwise tensor presheaf put $\widetilde f(x\otimes t)=t f(x)$ and then use module sheafification. Additivity and $\widetilde f(rx\otimes t)=t c(r)f(x)=\widetilde f(x\otimes c(r)t)$ give the balancing relation, and the formula commutes with restrictions. Conversely a $B$-linear map has this formula with $f(x)=\widetilde f(x\otimes1)$. Thus maps out of $E_cF$ are determined by their composites with $\eta_c:F\to\operatorname{Res}_cE_cF$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. This is a direct application of the two cited definitions' sectionwise construction and unique sheafification factorization.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: For an ideal subsheaf $L\subseteq A$, write $u_{L,F}:F\to F\otimes_A A/L$. The tensor-quotient lemma identifies this with the projection $F\to Q_L(F)$, up to its specified isomorphism, and says that $u_{L,F}$ is epic. Consequently an $A$-linear map $h:F\to H$ factors uniquely through $u_{L,F}$ precisely when $h(lx)=0$ for all local $l\in L$ and $x\in F$. Indeed such a map kills every finite sum of ideal multiples, hence the locally saturated product $LF$ by separatedness of $H$; it induces a map on the sectionwise quotient by $LF$, which extends uniquely to its sheafification. The converse follows from $u_{L,F}(lx)=x\otimes\bar l=0$. This uses the quotient construction, rather than any surjectivity of the quotient on sections.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text:
Fix one map $a:R\to S$, one ideal $I\subseteq R$, and one $R$-module sheaf $F$; put $J=a(I)S$, $Z=E_a(F\otimes_R R/I)$ and $W=(E_aF)\otimes_S S/J$. Define $t:F\to\operatorname{Res}_aW$ by $t(p)=(p\otimes1)\otimes\bar1$. For $i\in I$, balancing gives $t(ip)=(p\otimes a(i))\otimes\bar1=(p\otimes1)\otimes\overline{a(i)}=0$. Step 2 therefore gives $\bar t:F\otimes_R R/I\to\operatorname{Res}_aW$ with $\bar t(p\otimes\bar1)=t(p)$. Step 1 extends it to an $S$-linear map $\beta:Z\to W$. Its formula on the indicated original sections is
$$\beta((p\otimes\bar r)\otimes s)=s\bar t(rp\otimes\bar1)=(p\otimes s)\otimes\overline{a(r)}.$$
All uses of the quotient in this construction are licensed by the tensor-quotient lemma, and the extension is the sheafification factorization from Step 1.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text:
The $R$-linear map $F\to\operatorname{Res}_aZ$, $p\mapsto(p\otimes\bar1)\otimes1$, extends by Step 1 to $h:E_aF\to Z$, with $h(p\otimes s)=(p\otimes\bar1)\otimes s$. It is annihilated by each $a(i)$: on these tensors
$$h(a(i)(p\otimes s))=(ip\otimes\bar1)\otimes s=(p\otimes\bar i)\otimes s=0.$$
Step 1's uniqueness proves this equality as a map on $E_aF$. Since $J$ is locally generated by $a(I)$, $h$ kills all of $J(E_aF)$: each local finite sum of such multiples maps to zero by $S$-linearity, and the locally saturated hull maps to zero by separatedness of $Z$. Step 2 over $S$ gives a unique $S$-linear $\gamma:W\to Z$ with $\gamma((p\otimes s)\otimes\bar1)=(p\otimes\bar1)\otimes s$. In particular, for $v\in S$,
$$\gamma((p\otimes s)\otimes\bar v)=(p\otimes\bar1)\otimes sv.$$
Here $v$ is a section of $S$, with no requirement that it come from $R$.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: The maps $F\to Z$ and $F\to W$ sending $p$ to $((p\otimes\bar1)\otimes1)$ and $((p\otimes1)\otimes\bar1)$, respectively, detect equality of $S$-linear maps to any fixed target. For $Z$, first use Step 1 and then cancel the epic $u_{I,F}$ of Step 2. For $W$, first cancel $u_{J,E_aF}$ and then use Step 1. The formulas of Steps 3 and 4 show that $\gamma\beta$ and $\beta\gamma$ act identically on these two generating maps. They are therefore identities. This proves the required module isomorphism without imposing flatness or choosing representatives of arbitrary quotient sections.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: For any $R$-linear map $f:F\to G$, the two composites from $Z(F)$ to $W(G)$ in the naturality square both send the generating $p$ of Step 5 to $(f(p)\otimes1)\otimes\bar1$. The tensor-quotient lemma supplies the functorial quotient maps and their augmentation squares; uniqueness in Step 5 proves naturality. Thus this calculation applies in particular to every differential of a cochain complex, not merely to isomorphisms of modules.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: If $I'\subseteq I$, put $J'=a(I')S\subseteq J$. The tensor-quotient lemma gives the actual quotient transitions and $u_{I,F}= (1\otimes(R/I'\to R/I))u_{I',F}$, and the same identity over $S$. Starting from $p\in F$, either path in the square comparing $\beta_{I'}$ with $\beta_I$ therefore has value $(p\otimes1)\otimes\bar1$ in $W_I$. The generating map $F\to Z_{I'}$ detects equality by Step 5, so this transition square commutes. This explicitly uses the specified quotient transitions, rather than a replacement by any isomorphic tower.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: Apply Steps 3–7 degreewise to $F=P^k$, $k\in\mathbf Z$, and $I=I_n$, $n\geq1$. Step 6 with $f=d_P^k$ says exactly that $\beta_n$ and its inverse commute with differentials; with $f$ a component of a cochain map it proves naturality for such maps. Step 7 supplies the transition squares. By the definitions of a cochain map and a tower morphism, the resulting families are inverse morphisms of complexes of strict towers. Repeating the same construction for $b:S\to V$ and for $ba:R\to V$ gives $\beta_b$ and $\beta_{ba}$. Their target ideals agree because a local generator $b(a(i)s)v=(ba)(i)b(s)v$ belongs to $K$, and conversely each generator $(ba)(i)v$ is obtained with $s=1$; local saturation gives $b(J)V=K$. No degree bound or rank condition has entered.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: For completeness the balanced scalar associator itself is defined using Step 1 twice: the map $F\to\operatorname{Res}_{ba}E_{ba}F$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, extends to $E_bE_aF\to E_{ba}F$, with formula $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\mapsto p\otimes b(s)q$. Conversely extend $p\mapsto((p\otimes1)\otimes1)$ along $ba$ to obtain $p\otimes q\mapsto((p\otimes1)\otimes q)$. Both composites are identities by Step 1's uniqueness, applied twice on $E_bE_aF$ and once on $E_{ba}F$. The same uniqueness gives naturality for module maps; hence it also gives a cochain map and a strict tower map when applied termwise and to the quotient transitions. This constructs precisely the $\alpha$ appearing in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text:
Fix $k,n$. The source of the desired equation is $E_bE_a(P^k\otimes_R R/I_n)$. Equality of $V$-linear maps from this object is detected on $p\mapsto(((p\otimes\bar1)\otimes1)\otimes1)$, by Step 1 twice and the epic quotient augmentation of Step 2. More explicitly, on an original tensor $(((p\otimes\bar r)\otimes s)\otimes q)$ the left side first gives $(((p\otimes s)\otimes\overline{a(r)})\otimes q)$, then $((p\otimes s)\otimes q)\otimes\overline{(ba)(r)}$, and finally
$$(p\otimes b(s)q)\otimes\overline{(ba)(r)}.$$
The right side first gives $(p\otimes\bar r)\otimes b(s)q$ and then this identical displayed result. In particular they agree on the detecting generators, so the maps are equal. Steps 7–9 already proved that all four constituent families respect differentials and the actual transitions. Componentwise equality is therefore the stated strict tower equation, before any localization or inverse limit. In Lean the same detection is packaged by cancelling the twice-scalar-extended epic quotient augmentation: the augmentation compatibility formulas reduce both sides to the target augmentation composed with alpha, using naturality of alpha and of the target augmentation. This avoids expanding the tensor functors in the coherence calculation.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafified balanced tensor construction; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), universal property. Agent-written quotient-tower calculation.

proof.text: The scalar extension of the quotient augmentation sends $p\otimes s$ to $(p\otimes\bar1)\otimes s$; Step 3 sends this to $(p\otimes s)\otimes\bar1$, exactly the quotient augmentation of $E_aF$. Equality follows by Step 1, and the formulas for $b$ and $ba$ are identical with the corresponding letters. For $a=\mathrm{id}_R$, multiplication $E_{\mathrm{id}}F\to F$, $p\otimes r\mapsto rp$, is an isomorphism with inverse $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, by Step 1. Under these multiplication identifications the formula for $\beta$ sends $((p\otimes\bar r)\otimes s)$ to $sp\otimes\bar r$, the same as multiplication on its source; hence it becomes the identity on $F\otimes_R R/I$. These statements hold in every degree and at every tower index by Step 8. The argument used only the indicated universal properties and identities; it has no flatness, finite rank, boundedness, completion or derived-limit assumption. In Lean cancel the scalar-extended epic augmentation and use naturality of the multiplication comparison; transport along extension_id is reduced by equality induction. All local formulas and tower equations remain the displayed ones.

theorem ideal_quotient_tower_scalar_associator :
    ∃ (q : ∀ (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (I' I : RingedSiteIdeal R),
        IsContained I' I → (quotientCoefficient I' ⟶ quotientCoefficient I))
      (hmono : ∀ (R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (a : R ⟶ S)
        (I' I : RingedSiteIdeal R), IsContained I' I →
          IsContained (I'.extension a) (I.extension a))
      (hcomp : ∀ (R S V : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (a : R ⟶ S) (b : S ⟶ V)
        (I : RingedSiteIdeal R), (I.extension a).extension b = I.extension (a ≫ b))
      (hid : ∀ (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (I : RingedSiteIdeal R),
        I.extension (𝟙 R) = I)
      (uMap : ∀ (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (I : RingedSiteIdeal R),
        𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{u} (siteModuleRings R)) ⟶ idealTensorFunctor I)
      (α : ∀ (R S V : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (a : R ⟶ S) (b : S ⟶ V),
        SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor a ⋙
          SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor b ≅
            SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor (a ≫ b))
      (ε : ∀ R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u},
        SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor (𝟙 R) ≅
          𝟭 (SheafOfModules.{u} (siteModuleRings R)))
      (β : ∀ (R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (a : R ⟶ S) (I : RingedSiteIdeal R),
        idealTensorFunctor I ⋙ SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor a ≅
          SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.tensorFunctor a ⋙ idealTensorFunctor (I.extension a)),
    IdealScalarTransitionFormula q ∧
    IdealScalarUnitFormula uMap ∧
    IdealScalarAssociatorFormula α ∧
    IdealScalarIdentityFormula ε ∧
    IdealScalarQuotientFormula β ∧
    IdealScalarAugmentationCompatibility uMap β ∧
    IdealScalarTransitionCompatibility q hmono β ∧
    IdealScalarCompositionCompatibility hcomp α β ∧
    IdealScalarIdentityCompatibility hid ε β ∧
    IdealScalarTowerCompatibility q hmono β
